drhp.business: Dish TV India Limited provides direct-to-home satellite television broadcasting under the Dish TV, D2H and Zing Super brands, offering 600+ channels to households and establishments (hotels, restaurants, offices) across India. It has diversified into OTT content aggregation (Watcho, FLIQS), smart TVs (VZY), teleport services for broadcasters, and e-commerce (ShopZop) through its subsidiaries.
drhp.end_markets: India — tier I, tier II and non-urban regions|28 states and 8 union territories|individual households and establishments (hotels, restaurants, offices)
drhp.expansion: Dish TV entered the smart TV segment with VZY Smart TV (powered by Google TV) during September 2025, followed by regional rollouts in Kerala, and announced an enhanced South India offering in May 2026. It launched ShopZop, a B2B/B2C e-commerce platform, which went live on August 11, 2025 with over 4,000 listed products, and connected it with the VZY Smart TV ecosystem in September 2025. The Company also launched Content India, a physical and digital content trade hub, with an inaugural three-day event in Mumbai in March 2026, in partnership with C21 Media. The Company continued phasing out set-top-box subsidies to reduce capital expenditure on hardware.

litigation.note: MIB has issued repeated demand notices for DTH License Fee dating back to the license's 2003 issuance; the Company has challenged the demands before TDSAT (which stayed the original demand) and before the High Court of Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, with similar writs pending before the Supreme Court of India. Arguments before the High Court have concluded per the Board's Report/Corporate Overview section.

risks.note: Connected TVs, OTT platforms and internet-enabled streaming devices are disrupting DTH technology infrastructure, risking set-top-box hardware obsolescence and satellite capacity underutilization.

Operations are governed by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Ministry of Electronics and IT, and TRAI; changes in licensing norms, tariff regulations, content guidelines, spectrum policy or taxation can affect operations and profitability.

As a digital content distribution and DTH provider, the Company is exposed to data breaches, unauthorized access, network disruptions, service outages and ransomware attacks affecting customer trust and business continuity.
Geopolitical conflicts can raise input/commodity prices and trade barriers, while broader economic slowdowns can reduce consumer spending on entertainment.
Competition from OTT platforms, telecom operators and digital streaming services pressures subscriber growth, retention and revenue via changing consumer preferences and competitor pricing.

Media distribution infrastructure (broadcasting equipment, set-top boxes, IT equipment, content delivery technology, customer service centers and distribution network) requires substantial ongoing investment to stay current with technology.

MIB has raised repeated demand notices for DTH License Fee, with the latest (December 2025) claiming Rs 7,202.73 crore including interest; the matter is pending adjudication before the High Court of Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh and the Supreme Court of India.
The DTH industry faces a declining subscriber base industry-wide due to migration to OTT, shift to free-to-air platforms and rapid connected-TV adoption, a trend management expects to continue.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural decline in active pay-DTH subscribers industry-wide due to migration to OTT, shift to free-to-air platforms, and rising connected-TV adoption — expected to continue in coming years.
- New revenue streams from VZY Smart TV, ShopZop commissions and Content India partnerships/sponsorships are expected to offset declining DTH subscription revenue.
- Regional/vernacular content demand in South India, West Bengal, Odisha and Maharashtra is driving localized growth.
- Convergence of TV and OTT, and growth of connected-TV households, are reshaping distribution economics across the industry.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: Dish TV entered the smart TV segment with VZY Smart TV (powered by Google TV) during September 2025, followed by regional rollouts in Kerala, and announced an enhanced South India offering in May 2026. It launched ShopZop, a B2B/B2C e-commerce platform, which went live on August 11, 2025 with over 4,000 listed products, and connected it with the VZY Smart TV ecosystem in September 2025. The Company also launched Content India, a physical and digital content trade hub, with an inaugural three-day event in Mumbai in March 2026, in partnership with C21 Media. The Company continued phasing out set-top-box subsidies to reduce capital expenditure on hardware.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- scale: over 1044 MHz of satellite bandwidth capacity — evidence: "the company has a massive bandwidth capacity of over 1044 MHz powered by satellites" — against it: DTH subscriptions and revenue declined 25.84% YoY on subscriber churn
- distribution: network of over 2,000 distributors and more than 1,00,000 dealers/retailers across 9,500 towns — evidence: "a vast distribution network comprising over 2,000 distributors and more than 1,00,000 dealers across 9,500 towns of the country"
- integration: single sign-in OTT aggregation (Watcho) bundling 25+ third-party OTT apps with linear DTH — evidence: "embedded its Watcho app into cloud-TV operated smart TVs, allowing a single login and subscription besides 25+ popular OTT apps options"
- licence/regulatory: 20-year DTH License from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting — evidence: "the amended guidelines... provide for a term of 20 years for the DTH License" — against it: MIB has raised a cumulative license-fee claim of Rs 7,202.73 crore under a December 2025 demand, currently under litigation

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Connected TVs, OTT platforms and internet-enabled streaming devices are disrupting DTH technology infrastructure, risking set-top-box hardware obsolescence and satellite capacity underutilization.
- Operations are governed by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Ministry of Electronics and IT, and TRAI; changes in licensing norms, tariff regulations, content guidelines, spectrum policy or taxation can affect operations and profitability.
- As a digital content distribution and DTH provider, the Company is exposed to data breaches, unauthorized access, network disruptions, service outages and ransomware attacks affecting customer trust and business continuity.
- Geopolitical conflicts can raise input/commodity prices and trade barriers, while broader economic slowdowns can reduce consumer spending on entertainment.
- Competition from OTT platforms, telecom operators and digital streaming services pressures subscriber growth, retention and revenue via changing consumer preferences and competitor pricing.
- Media distribution infrastructure (broadcasting equipment, set-top boxes, IT equipment, content delivery technology, customer service centers and distribution network) requires substantial ongoing investment to stay current with technology.
- MIB has raised repeated demand notices for DTH License Fee, with the latest (December 2025) claiming Rs 7,202.73 crore including interest; the matter is pending adjudication before the High Court of Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh and the Supreme Court of India.
- The DTH industry faces a declining subscriber base industry-wide due to migration to OTT, shift to free-to-air platforms and rapid connected-TV adoption, a trend management expects to continue.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Build a comprehensive content ecosystem — Content India, launched with C21 Media, aims to connect content buyers, creators and tech companies for cross-border content sourcing and diversification.
- Shift towards hybrid entertainment by scaling VZY Smart TV (Google TV-powered, integrating streaming apps with live TV) and Dish TV Smart+ to phase out set-top-box dependence.
- Lead the transition from set-top boxes to smart screens in media distribution, aligning strategy with converging linear broadcast and streaming.
- Deepen the super-app experience on Watcho and integrate third-party OTT (e.g., Amazon Prime Video) across Dish TV, Watcho and VZY Smart TVs.
- Expand distribution at the micro (Tehsil) level by engaging more partners and freelancers to reach rural and semi-urban areas.
